paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐκύκλωσα ἕως τόπου ὅπου οὐδὲν ἐποίηται.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ekyklōsa heōs topou hopou ouden epoiētai.

i18n.en: And I went round about as far as a place where nothing is made.

notes.official: Enoch's tour reaches the cosmographic-confinement-site of the stars who transgressed the commandment of the Lord. The fallen-stars framework integrates astronomical-regularity with cosmic-moral-obligation — the stars who 'failed to come forth in their appointed times' are bound as cosmic-rebels. The framework develops at length in the Astronomical Book (1 En 72-82, Ship B). See central entry `fallen-stars-prison-1-enoch-18-21-jude-6-2-pet-2-4-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ εἶδον ἐκεῖ φοβερὸν ἔργον· οὐκ οὐρανὸν ὕψος οὔτε γῆν τεθεμελιωμένην, ἀλλὰ τόπον ἀκατασκεύαστον καὶ φοβερόν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eidon ekei phoberon ergon; ouk ouranon hypsos oute gēn tethemeliōmenēn, alla topon akataskeuaston kai phoberon.

i18n.en: And I saw there a terrible thing: no height of heaven, no earth firmly founded, but an unformed and terrible place.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐκεῖ εἶδον ἑπτὰ ἀστέρας τοῦ οὐρανοῦ δεδεμένους ἐν αὐτῷ ὁμοίους ὄρεσι μεγάλοις, καὶ ἐν πυρὶ καιομένους.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ekei eidon hepta asteras tou ouranou dedemenous en autō homoious oresi megalois, kai en pyri kaiomenous.

i18n.en: And there I saw seven stars of heaven bound in it, like great mountains, and burning in fire.

paragraphs.text: Τότε εἶπον· Διὰ ποίαν αἰτίαν δέδενται καὶ διὰ τί ὧδε ἐρρίφησαν;
paragraphs.translit: Tote eipon; Dia poian aitian dedentai kai dia ti hōde errhiphēsan?

i18n.en: Then I said: For what cause are they bound, and why have they been cast here?

paragraphs.text: Τότε εἶπέν μοι Οὐριήλ, ὁ εἷς τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων, ὃς μετ' ἐμοῦ ἦν καὶ αὐτὸς ἡγεῖτο αὐτῶν, καὶ εἶπεν· Ἑνώχ, διὰ τί ἐρωτᾷς καὶ διὰ τί ἀνερευνᾷς καὶ φιλομαθεῖς;
paragraphs.translit: Tote eipen moi Ouriēl, ho heis tōn hagiōn angelōn, hos met' emou ēn kai autos hēgeito autōn, kai eipen; Henōch, dia ti erōtas kai dia ti anereunas kai philomatheis?

i18n.en: Then Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me and who was leading them, said to me: Enoch, why do you ask, and why do you search out, and why are you eager for knowledge?

paragraphs.text: Οὗτοί εἰσιν τῶν ἀστέρων τοῦ οὐρανοῦ οἱ παραβάντες τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ἐδέθησαν ὧδε μέχρι τοῦ τελειῶσαι μυρίων χιλιάδων ἐτῶν τοῦ χρόνου τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Houtoi eisin tōn asterōn tou ouranou hoi parabantes tēn entolēn tou kyriou kai edethēsan hōde mechri tou teleiōsai myriōn chiliadōn etōn tou chronou tōn hamartēmatōn autōn.

i18n.en: These are of the stars of heaven, those who transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and they were bound here until the completion of ten thousand thousands of years, the time of their transgressions.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἀπῆλθον εἰς ἄλλον τόπον, φοβερώτερον τοῦ ἐκείνου· εἶδον δὲ φοβερὸν θέαμα, πῦρ μέγα ἐκεῖ καιόμενον καὶ φλεγόμενον, καὶ διαιρέσεις εἶχεν ὁ τόπος καὶ τέλος εἶχεν ἕως τῆς ἀβύσσου, μεστὸς στύλων πυρὸς μεγάλων καταφερομένων· οὔτε μέτρον αὐτοῦ οὔτε μέγεθος ἠδυνάμην ἰδεῖν, οὔτε εἰκάσαι.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ekeithen apēlthon eis allon topon, phoberōteron tou ekeinou; eidon de phoberon theama, pyr mega ekei kaiomenon kai phlegomenon, kai diaireseis eichen ho topos kai telos eichen heōs tēs abyssou, mestos stylōn pyros megalōn katapheromenōn; oute metron autou oute megethos ēdynamēn idein, oute eikasai.

i18n.en: And from there I went to another place, more terrible than the former; and I saw a terrible sight — a great fire there burning and blazing — and the place had divisions and reached to the abyss, full of great pillars of fire descending. Its measure and its size I could not see, nor could I conjecture.

paragraphs.text: Τότε εἶπον· Ὡς φοβερὸς ὁ τόπος καὶ ὡς δεινὸς εἰς θεωρίαν.
paragraphs.translit: Tote eipon; Hōs phoberos ho topos kai hōs deinos eis theōrian.

i18n.en: Then I said: How terrible is this place, and how dreadful to behold!

paragraphs.text: Τότε ἀπεκρίθη μοι Οὐριήλ, ὁ εἷς τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων ὃς μετ' ἐμοῦ ἦν, καὶ εἶπέν μοι· Ἑνώχ, διὰ τί φόβον τοιοῦτον ἔχεις καὶ τρόμον; Καὶ ἀπεκρίθην· Διὰ τὸν τόπον τὸν φοβερὸν τοῦτον καὶ διὰ τὴν θεωρίαν τοῦ ἀλγηδόνος.
paragraphs.translit: Tote apekrithē moi Ouriēl, ho heis tōn hagiōn angelōn hos met' emou ēn, kai eipen moi; Henōch, dia ti phobon toiouton echeis kai tromon? Kai apekrithēn; Dia ton topon ton phoberon touton kai dia tēn theōrian tou algēdonos.

i18n.en: Then Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered me and said: Enoch, why do you have such fear and trembling? And I answered: Because of this terrible place, and because of the sight of pain.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ εἶπεν· Οὗτος ὁ τόπος δεσμωτήριον τῶν ἀγγέλων ἐστὶν, καὶ ὧδε συσχεθήσονται ἕως αἰῶνος.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eipen; Houtos ho topos desmōtērion tōn angelōn estin, kai hōde syschethēsontai heōs aiōnos.

i18n.en: And he said: This place is the prison of the angels, and here they shall be kept forever.
